greeting: Good morning, Rick! Grab your coffee, here's what's new in tech today.

items.title: Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia CEO
items.note: Nvidia's founder resigned this morning after a scandal over affairs, and the company's finance chief, Colette Kress, is filling in as CEO. Nvidia makes the chips behind most AI and is worth more than $4 trillion.

items.title: Google brings the Gemini app to Apple CarPlay
items.note: You can now talk to Google's Gemini assistant hands-free on your car's screen. Just update the Gemini app on your iPhone and it shows up in CarPlay.

items.title: AirTag 2, AirPods and MacBook Air deals
items.note: Amazon's early Black Friday sale has a 4-pack of AirTag 2 for $70 and AirPods Pro 3 for $199. Some M5 MacBook Airs are $250 off too.

items.title: United is restricting AI agents from booking flights
items.note: AI assistants can still look up United flights, but the airline says a real person has to finish the booking. It worries about security and rules like the bag safety questions only a human can answer.

items.title: Toyota brings back Scion with a tiny 25-mph kei truck
items.note: The little KEI-01 is a low-speed work truck, like a street-legal golf cart with a 600-pound bed and all-wheel drive. It will be put together in Indiana and sold to fleets like farms and campuses starting in 2027.

items.title: Google's new smart glasses arrive next month
items.note: Warby Parker and Gentle Monster frames with Google's Gemini built in go on sale December 10, starting at $395. CNET tried them and loved the live translation that speaks other languages into your ear.

items.title: Apple's new holiday ad features the MacBook Neo
items.note: A short, sweet film about a kid who turns her drawings into a cartoon. Watch for a cameo from an old iPhone 3GS.

items.title: Apple is closing its Support Community forum on November 20
items.note: The user forum that often pops up when you search for an iPhone problem will stop taking new questions. Old answers stay readable, and Apple points people to its official support site instead.
